name: United States federal

registry.title: IRS employer identification number, not state entity registration

estimated_tax.title: Pay as you go: estimated tax payment dates

obligations.title: Individual estimated tax payment 1
obligations.applies_when: Individuals who must make estimated tax payments, including self-employed individuals
obligations.due_rule: April 15; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote:
April 15 for income earned January 1 to March 31

If these due dates fall on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the payments are due the next business day.

obligations.title: Individual estimated tax payment 2
obligations.applies_when: Individuals who must make estimated tax payments, including self-employed individuals
obligations.due_rule: June 15; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote:
June 15 for income earned April 1 to May 31

If these due dates fall on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the payments are due the next business day.

obligations.title: Individual estimated tax payment 3
obligations.applies_when: Individuals who must make estimated tax payments, including self-employed individuals
obligations.due_rule: September 15; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote:
September 15 for income earned June 1 to August 31

If these due dates fall on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the payments are due the next business day.

obligations.title: Individual estimated tax payment 4
obligations.applies_when: Individuals who must make estimated tax payments, including self-employed individuals
obligations.due_rule: January 15 of the following year; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote:
January 15 of the following year for income earned September 1 to December 31

If these due dates fall on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the payments are due the next business day.

obligations.title: File and furnish nonemployee compensation information
obligations.applies_when: Businesses making reportable nonemployee compensation payments, subject to exceptions and reporting threshold
obligations.due_rule: January 31 following the payment year; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote: File Form 1099-NEC with Form 1096, Annual Summary and Transmittal of U.S. Information Returns, must be filed with the IRS and provided to recipients by Jan. 31.

obligations.title: Nonemployee compensation reporting threshold by payment year
obligations.applies_when: Trade or business payments reportable on Form 1099-NEC; backup withholding can require reporting regardless of amount
obligations.due_rule: Apply the threshold for the payment year before preparing the annual information return
obligations.quote: For payments made before 2026, the reporting threshold is $600. For payments made in 2026, the reporting threshold is $2,000. For payments made after 2026, see Pub. 1099 for the inflation-adjusted reporting threshold.

obligations.title: File and furnish wage statements
obligations.applies_when: Employers reporting employee wages and employment taxes withheld
obligations.due_rule: January 31 following the wage year; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote:
Forms filed annually with a due date of Jan. 31

File Forms W-2 with Form W-3 with the SSA to report wages paid and employment taxes withheld from these wages during the previous tax year. Forms W-2 are required to be provided to employees by Jan. 31.

obligations.title: Employer quarterly federal tax return
obligations.applies_when: Employers paying wages subject to employment taxes; approved annual filers and agricultural employers have separate rules
obligations.due_rule: April 30, July 31, October 31, January 31 for prior quarter; next business day if weekend or legal holiday; 10 additional calendar days if all taxes timely deposited
obligations.quote:
Forms filed quarterly with due dates of April 30, July 31, Oct. 31 and Jan. 31 (for the fourth quarter of the previous calendar year)

File Form 941 if you paid wages subject to employment taxes with the IRS for each quarter by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. If you timely deposited all taxes when due, then you have 10 additional calendar days to file the return.

obligations.title: S corporation income tax return after an accepted election
obligations.applies_when: A corporation or other entity whose Form 2553 election was accepted by the IRS and remains in effect
obligations.due_rule: Generally the 15th day of the 3rd month after the tax year ends; next business day if Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday
obligations.quote:
A corporation or other entity must file Form 1120-S if (a) it elected to be an S corporation by filing Form 2553, (b) the IRS accepted the election, and (c) the election remains in effect.

Generally, an S corporation must file Form 1120-S by the 15 day of the 3rd month after the end of its tax year.

obligations.title: Schedule C business income and Schedule SE self-employment tax
obligations.applies_when: Self-employed sole proprietors and gig workers, subject to filing requirements
obligations.form: Schedule C (Form 1040) and Schedule SE (Form 1040 or 1040-SR)
obligations.due_rule: File with the annual income tax return; estimated payments have separate quarterly deadlines
obligations.quote:
Self-employed individuals generally must pay self-employment (SE) tax as well as income tax.

To file your annual income tax return, you will need to use Schedule C (Form 1040), Profit or Loss from Business (Sole Proprietorship), to report any income or loss from a business you operated or profession you practiced as a sole proprietor, or gig work performed.

Use the income or loss calculated on Schedule C to calculate the amount of Social Security and Medicare taxes you should have paid during the year.

notes: Selected federal obligations only, not a complete compliance checklist. The registry source is EIN registration, not business formation. Form 2553 makes the S corporation election; Form 1120-S is the return after an accepted election. Quarterly dates are general dates, subject to weekends, legal holidays and special relief. Tax deposits have different deadlines from returns. The 1099 threshold is $600 before 2026, $2,000 in 2026, with inflation adjustment after 2026. Check the current-year instructions; do not apply the 2026 amount automatically to later years.
